story.what_it_does: Atul is a chemicals group. In FY2025-26, about 29% of its revenue came from Life Science Chemicals and 71% from Performance and Other Chemicals. Group revenue from operations was ₹6,273.54 crore.
story.plans: The company expects two new Aromatics-II projects to be operationalised in 2026-27. Group capital spending fell to ₹145.49 crore in 2025-26 from ₹216.16 crore a year earlier.
story.moat: The notes do not describe a clear competitive advantage. The company says it has effectively zero debt, and its operating margin was 19.66%. It faces pressure from Chinese pesticide oversupply and soft export demand.

scenarios.story: The two new Aromatics-II projects start up in 2026-27 and Polymers - Performance Materials keeps growing, as it did with 18% sales growth in FY2025-26. Revenue growth continues from ₹5,583.35 crore to ₹6,273.54 crore.
signals_to_watch: Two new Aromatics-II projects operationalised in 2026-27
Polymers - Performance Materials sales growth after the 18% in 2025-26

scenarios.story: Revenue keeps growing modestly, with margins near the FY2025-26 levels of 19.66% operating and 10.99% net. Return on net worth stays around 11.53% as the company works through mixed demand.
signals_to_watch: Pharmaceuticals and Aromatics sales change after the 6% in 2025-26

scenarios.story: Chinese pesticide oversupply and soft export demand squeeze sales realisations and market share, and US tariffs keep hurting Aromatics-II sales outside India. Unresolved items such as overdue loans and disputed tax demands could add further strain.
signals_to_watch: Oversupply of pesticides from China affecting sales realisations and market share
Loans overdue over 90 days (₹28.76 crore at March 31, 2026) and the Anaven LLP loan extension
